episodes.title: Repo at 5.50%: The First Hike Since February 2023
episodes.subtitle: On 7 October 2026 the RBI MPC raised the repo rate by 25 bps to 5.50% and moved the stance to calibrated tightening. A composite consumer CFO must price a 15 October reset before the board sits on the 16th.
episodes.description: HBS-style teaching case dated 9 October 2026. Public facts from the RBI Monetary Policy Statement of 7 October 2026: unanimous +25 bps to 5.50% repo; SDF 5.25%; MSF and Bank Rate 5.75%; stance to calibrated tightening (Business Standard: 4-2). First hike since February 2023 after 125 bps of easing from 6.50% to 5.25%. FY27 GDP forecast raised to 7.1% from 6.7%; FY27 CPI to 5.2% from 5.0%; headline CPI expected to average almost 5.8% over the next three quarters; core 4.4%. Forex reserves $734.6 bn as of 2 October; net FDI $13.8 bn April-August; FPI outflows $10.3 bn; credit growth 18.1% (Mint) / 18-19% (Deputy Governor Swaminathan J). Composite firm: Malabar Consumer Products Ltd. Composite CFO: Meera Iyer.
sources: Reserve Bank of India, Monetary Policy Statement, 2026-27, Resolution of the MPC, 5-7 October 2026.
Reserve Bank of India, Governor's Statement, 7 October 2026, Sanjay Malhotra.
Reserve Bank of India, Money Market Operations as on 7 October 2026 (8 October release).
The Hindu; Business Standard; BusinessLine; Mint; Businessworld; CNBC-TV18, 7 October 2026.

episodes.title: The First Hike in Nearly Four Years
episodes.subtitle: On 7 October 2026 the RBI MPC raised the repo rate 25 bps to 5.50% and shifted stance to calibrated tightening. A composite castings CFO must reprice floating working capital, the August capex note, and covenant headroom before the board meets.
episodes.category: Monetary Policy, Cost of Capital and CFO Judgment
episodes.description: HBS-style teaching case dated 8 October 2026. Public facts from the RBI Monetary Policy Statement, 5 to 7 October 2026, the Governor's statement, The Hindu and Reuters. MPC unanimously raised the LAF repo by 25 bps to 5.50%. SDF 5.25%. MSF and Bank Rate 5.75%. Stance changed from neutral to calibrated tightening. Rate cuts off the table in the near term. Prior easing cycle cut 125 bps from 6.50% to 5.25% by December 2025, then four holds. Reuters: FY inflation forecast lifted to 5.2% from 5%; real GDP forecast to 7.1% from 6.7%. Governor: headline CPI expected to average almost 5.8% over the next three quarters; core inflation 4.4% this year. Composite firm: Narmada Alloys Pvt. Ltd. Composite decision-maker: CFO Arvind Deshmukh. Not a real filing.
sources: Reserve Bank of India, Monetary Policy Statement, 2026-27, Resolution of the Monetary Policy Committee, October 5 to 7, 2026. Unanimous 25 bps hike in LAF repo to 5.50%; SDF 5.25%; MSF and Bank Rate 5.75%; stance changed to calibrated tightening.

Statement by Shri Sanjay Malhotra, Governor, RBI, 7 October 2026, and RBI YouTube live statement. Rate cuts off the table; next action a hike or a pause; stance change by a majority of 4-2; headline CPI expected to average almost 5.8% over the next three quarters; core inflation 4.4% this financial year.
The Hindu, 7 October 2026: first hike after the December 2025 cut to 5.25% and four subsequent holds; easing cycle of 125 bps from 6.50% to 5.25%.

Reuters, 7 October 2026: inflation forecast raised to 5.2% from 5%; GDP growth forecast raised to 7.1% from 6.7%; Sakshi Gupta, HDFC Bank, expects another 50-75 bps. Analyst view, not an RBI projection.
RBI, Monetary Policy Statement, August 3 to 5, 2026: repo held at 5.25%; stance neutral; GDP 6.7% and CPI 5.0% projections that the October resolution revises.

episodes.subtitle: RBI repo held at 5.25% with a neutral stance. A composite auto-component CFO still has to reprice the unhedged import book, the floating-rate interest line, and the hurdle rate before Wednesday's board.

episodes.title: Who Holds the Kill Switch?
episodes.subtitle: RBI’s 24 June 2026 draft Guidance on Regulatory Principles for Model Risk Management is still a draft on 3 October. A CFO must inventory, validate, and be able to stop every model — including the vendor’s.

episodes.title: When Scope 3 Outruns the P&L
episodes.subtitle: IIM Bangalore’s FY 2024–25 BRSR study, SEBI’s FY 2026–27 assurance glide path, and the mid-cap CFO who still treats carbon as a footnote
episodes.description: An HBS-style teaching case set on 2 September 2026. After IIM Bangalore’s Supply Chain Management Centre published an analysis of 982 BRSR filings for FY 2024–25, and with SEBI’s BRSR Core assessment-or-assurance obligation reaching the top 1,000 listed entities in FY 2026–27, a composite mid-cap foundry CFO must recommend whether the board files and finishes, opens Scope 3 slowly, puts carbon and water into the capital plan, or waits for a peer. All national statistics and legal waypoints are taken from public sources.

episodes.title: The Reporting Map Is Not One Map
episodes.subtitle: How a global CFO files climate data when Washington proposes rescission, Sacramento still wants Scope 1 and 2 by 10 November, and ISSB keeps spreading
episodes.description: An HBS-style teaching case set on 2 September 2026. After the SEC proposed full rescission of its 2024 climate rules and CARB moved the first SB 253 Scope 1 and 2 filing to 10 November 2026, a composite mid-cap industrial CFO must choose a reporting architecture across California, ISSB markets, and a narrowed CSRD. Real Commission releases, CARB notices, Council votes and Faber’s Frankfurt count are woven through a classroom decision.

episodes.title: The Calendar Decision: Should a CFO Elect Semiannual Reporting?
episodes.subtitle: SEC File No. S7-2026-15, a 97 percent comment-file revolt, and the board posture that will not wait
episodes.description: An HBS-style case set on 1 September 2026. After the SEC proposed letting U.S. public companies replace Form 10-Q with a semiannual Form 10-S, and after a historically lopsided comment file closed 97 percent opposed, a mid-cap industrial CFO must recommend whether her board should pre-commit to quarterly reporting, prepare to elect, wait for a first cohort, or set a liquidity trigger. Real Commission statements, comment statistics, and CFA survey findings are woven through a teaching composite so students decide.

episodes.title: AI ROI Blind Spot: Protiviti Survey
episodes.subtitle: Why many finance leaders still struggle to measure returns on AI investments
episodes.description: A recent Protiviti survey highlights a critical blind spot: while organisations continue to invest heavily in AI, many CFOs and finance teams still lack clear frameworks to measure and report AI returns. This episode helps students understand how future finance leaders should approach AI investment decisions, measurement, and governance.

episodes.title: AI ROI Paradox in Finance
episodes.subtitle: When heavy AI investment meets uncertain returns — what should a CFO do?
episodes.description: Today’s episode examines the growing paradox facing finance leaders: significant investment in AI tools and infrastructure is being made, yet clear, measurable returns remain elusive for many organisations. Students learn how a CFO should evaluate AI spend, measure value, and decide when to scale or pause.

episodes.title: The $3.2 Trillion Question Hiding in Plain Sight
episodes.subtitle: NVIDIA’s Record Quarter and the Off-Balance-Sheet AI Infrastructure Commitments of the AI-7
episodes.description: NVIDIA reported record Q2 FY2027 results while research revealed that the AI-7 companies now carry approximately $3.2 trillion in contractual commitments largely sitting in footnotes. This episode teaches students how to read true committed capital, utilisation risk, and the difference between reported leverage and reality.
